Using lattice QCD, a comprehensive investigation of two-current correlations in pions is conducted across the entire spectrum of relevant local and non-local pair operators in mesons. By employing a maximum entropy ansatz to approximate the determinant of the matrix of operators on the lattice, relevant association parameters are extracted and accurately reproduce lattice data for the mass and decay constant of pions. A simplified effective field theory, known as linear sigma model, is also analyzed in comparison to lattice results and reveals that the quark condensate and quark mass are directly related to the association parameters derived from lattice calculations.

Disks surrounding young stars show a wide range of accretion rates, with rates from low mass stars being particularly higher than those from T Tauri stars. To investigate this distinction, researchers examined the reflectivity spectra of accretion shocks, using a subset of 11 sources from the PENELLOPE project. They focused on a specific variable object, XX Cha, and analyzed 240 spectra obtained over a short time frame, revealing extreme variations in gas velocities and flow rates. As a result, the accretion rates of objects like XX Cha contribute significantly to the broad distribution of observed flow rates. The characteristics of variable objects, which make up about 10% of the sample, may also suggest that these objects have unique properties that require further investigation.

In offline single-agent reinforcement learning, an intriguing scenario arises where the behavior policy and value function of an agent are independent, an setting that models scenarios such as training a taxi driver with drivers who adhere to traffic laws. Offline multi-agent reinforcement learning typically involves a common dataset where an entity either shares an environment or learns from aggregated data, and we investigate this scenario when all agents have distinct value functions and cannot share experiences with one another in the same time step. We establish a theoretical connection between these two independent settings that cannot be contradicted. A taxi driver and a fleet of drivers who follow the same policy, in the same environment, in the same location. A novel offline multi-agent problem where distinct value functions and learning from diverse policies with independent settings. Offline single-agent and offline multi-agent reinforcement learning. Policy generation from diverse learning settings.

We developed a novel approach for aligning images by utilizing 2D megavoltage images and combining convolutional neural networks with a traditional alignment method known as the active contour model. Our approach involves using a CNN to generate initial starting points for the contour model, which then refines the parameter estimates through an iterative process. We evaluated our method on synthetic images and real images acquired from cancer patients undergoing radiation therapy treatment. Results showed that our CNN-based approach yields more accurate and consistent image alignments when compared to the standard contour model alone, particularly in terms of consistent results across different images. Our findings also highlight the potential for CNNs to be used for a wide range of medical image alignments, which could support the field of radiation therapy research and beyond.

We demonstrate that single-particle entanglement must yield genuinely nonlocal phenomena, specifically, the ability for a local measurement on a single particle to steer another, spatially separated particle, even without trusting the equipment used. By developing a nontrivial definition of single-particle entanglement that considers the inability to describe particles using a localized basis, we show that entangled states can be harnessed to nonlocally steer uncorrelated, randomly produced particles. Notably, we find that nonlocal steering can be used as a resource to achieve tasks impossible with classical correlations, providing a practical distinction between single-particle entanglement and classical particle coherence.

The integration of learning algorithms into Internet of Vehicles systems has encountered several challenges, including data privacy concerns, manipulation risks, and centralization issues. Researchers have explored various technologies to address these problems, with significant results achieved using secure computation and blockchain technologies. However, a paper-based federally learned infrastructure for Internet of Vehicles has not been thoroughly reviewed in the literature. Our research focuses on conducting a comprehensive review of blockchain-enabled federally learned Internet of Vehicles systems. We examine essential federally learned components for Internet of Vehicles, describe various learning attacks, review blockchain fundamentals, and explore the advantages of using blockchain technology in these systems. We categorize the reviewed systems according to their learning approaches and network architectures. Moreover, we examine the critical criteria for evaluating these systems, discuss various learning attacks that are mitigated, and outline several promising research directions. Specifically, we propose a novel blockchain-enabled federally learned system where mobile devices update a reference model that is then shared with vehicle systems to enhance efficiency. Our review is meant to highlight the potential of blockchain technology in creating secure and decentralized learning frameworks for Internet of Vehicles systems and to outline several promising research directions.

V392 Persei, previously recognized as a dwarf nova that had recently experienced an outburst, was surprisingly detected emitting \gamma-rays just 11 days after a bright optical nova event. This initial \gamma-ray signal swiftly declined within approximately 10 days. Earlier observations had failed to establish the nature of this system, with some speculation suggesting it might be an X-ray binary involving a magnetar. By analyzing existing data, we determined the most probable explanation for the nova eruption involves an accreting white dwarf, supported by observations showing periodic variations with a 0.197-day cycle during the X-ray phase. Observations also revealed unusually high ejecta masses and luminosity, along with an exceptionally late decline stage onset. This late onset could be attributed to the dense stellar wind from the binary system, potentially originating from the accretion disk's outer edge. Investigating the far-ultraviolet emission yielded unexpected findings, with the total energy released in UV radiation exceeding that in X-rays. This suggests the X-rays and \gamma-rays might be absorbed within the system, and further observations in these wavelengths could be crucial for comprehending the complex emission mechanisms at work in dense stellar wind novae.

A significant amount of research has been conducted in the fields of full-duplex and device-to-device (D2D) communications to enhance mobile network efficiency and spectrum usage. These approaches rely on user equipment with advanced capabilities, which may not be readily available in current commercial systems. To explore full/D2D feedback possibilities with standard user equipment, this paper presents a feasible feedback method that includes a codebook and encoding technique for MIMO systems. This codebook and encoding technique can also be utilized by conventional user equipment without requiring specialized capabilities. Furthermore, we propose an efficient method to create the codebook and encoding technique that minimizes the error between the desired and reconstructed signals, utilizing a generalized minimum variance approach. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique when compared to existing approaches.

In a periodic structure without symmetry, we investigate the conservation of the Henderson momentum in a 2D system that is subject to time-varying forces, revealing how it accounts for the persistent, counterclocklet-like, and counterclockwise surface currents found both inside and near holes of a 3D Hofstadter lattice. This discovery holds true even without the assumption of the Henderson momentum being a robust, topological property. Consequently, this finding extends to a broader category of models that exhibit counterclocklet-like and counterclockwise surface currents in their highest and lowest energy bands, including the generalized multi-component SSH models in 3D with multiple components.

For as long as a star remains in a quasar state, it is thought that it can effectively regulate the flow of accreted matter by releasing powerful quasar winds. In the case of certain dense areas within the universe, where the rate of matter being pulled in by gravity exceeds the rate of matter being expelled by quasar winds, it is hypothesized that this could lead to a self-punishing mechanism that ultimately flattens out the distribution of these areas for a period of time. To examine this theory, we developed a mathematical model that we applied to the data from the Planck satellite to establish both upper and lower limits on how much mass can be lost through quasar winds, which will be valuable for astronomers studying these unique phenomena in the universe.

The earliest galaxies likely contained dense clusters of stars around their galactic centers, and a type of star known as Population III probably lived within these groups. These stars have massive weights and can produce significant gravitational waves as they move through dense clusters. As a result, detectors like LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA may have been able to pick up signals from merging black holes formed from these PIII stars. However, scientists are unsure if they could have. To address this uncertainty, researchers have examined the possible PIII star remnants in clusters of star around the Milky Way, Andromeda, and M33. They found that massive black holes and neutron stars moving at high speeds have a high probability of colliding with each other or with lighter objects, producing detectable gravitational waves in about half of the scenarios they studied. Unfortunately, these events may have occurred too long ago for current detectors to detect. Nevertheless, if more modern detectors like KAGRA, LIGO-India, and a upgraded LIGO come online, scientists have a better chance of detecting these gravitational waves, and could even locate the home of these early galaxies.

In modern high-speed wireless networks, ensuring secure data transmission is a pressing concern. To achieve this, physical layer security techniques rely on the fact that eavesdroppers have limited physical reach. In this paper, physical layer security analysis is applied to a wireless transmission system with an out-of-range malicious listener and accessible base stations and receiver. The system uses a multi-carrier transmission protocol and an intermediate relay node to forward data. The rate at which information can be securely transmitted is calculated for both single-user and user-multiplexing scenarios. Notably, there is no optimal single-user link because increasing signal frequencies causes the communication channel to become less secure, resulting in lower achievable rates. The paper also provides comparison theorets with related works.

Text-based adventure games provide a fast and effective way to practice real-world tasks for virtual assistants. The rate at which these games operate is extremely high, allowing for one hundred thousand steps per second on average. Our new benchmark, TextWorldExpress, raises the requirement to complete one second tasks. It consists of twelve variants, matching the original TextWorld dataset in terms of complexity but with a twelve times larger number of problems. We provide four different sets of challenges, gradually increasing in difficulty. As expected, being able to complete the simpler problems within one second is even difficult for the most advanced methods. To achieve the highest scores on our benchmark, we propose a baselines that can solve one million problems per second.

Deep learning, particularly through recurrent neural networks (LSTMs), has achieved remarkable success in various video analysis tasks. However, the substantial computational requirements of these algorithms present significant challenges. This research introduces an innovative approach that combines algorithmic and hardware optimizations to create a real-time video sequence application. The proposed method features a novel hardware design known as a LSTM-enabled Video Sequence System (LIVIS). The LIVIS system incorporates a hardware-accelerated LSTM module, a unique activation function, and an efficient storage architecture to enable the detection of specific events in video sequences. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the LIVIS system's capability to accurately detect events in video sequences with high speed. The results obtained from this study include the detection of sports such as soccer, basketball, and volleyball in video sequences. The achieved performance metrics, namely a processing speed of 24.14 frames per second and an energy efficiency of 0.024 picojoules per frame, highlight the potential of this algorithm and hardware协同 approach for practical video analysis applications.

If we consider a state in a conformal field theory that has no external gravitating fields and is invariant under rotations, we can focus on two specific parts of the theory: a set of anti-convex operators and another that is strictly convex. We prove that any collection of operators that is convex can be ignored, leading to the conclusion that states in these types of CFTs must follow a specific "feeble gravity conjecture," which suggests a limit on how much non-convexity is allowed in relation to any degree of convexity. Our findings are further illustrated by examining the 3D Ising model and the O(N) model in three dimensions.

We establish a connection between the positive tight Hilbert polynomial of parameter quotients and the purity of the parameter ideal for local rings, providing an equivalent condition to this purity in terms of the tight ring. Additionally, we demonstrate the existence of a threshold $c > 0$ where the positive Hilbert polynomial implies the birational normality of large power quotients of an ideal, which in turn is equivalent to the triviality of local cohomology $H^1_I(\omega_R)$. These findings hold true for $F$-regular local rings when replacing asymptotic and positive asymptotic behavior. Notably, it becomes trivial that the vanishing of $H^1_I(\omega_R)$ results in the tight polynomial being positive, which implies $F$-regularity.

The rapid expansion of auxiliary services in data centers and networks necessitates innovative policy frameworks to ensure efficient infrastructure utilization. To capture the service data center market interactions accurately, we developed a quadratic cost model and applied it to evaluate existing policies, including price caps, supply caps, auxiliary service sharing, and performance optimization protocols. However, none of these policies prove superior universally, with optimal outcomes varying across different market conditions. Consequently, we recommend condition-based policy design, tailored to specific market scenarios, such as setting supply caps when auxiliary providers possess significant market power, or allowing temporary excess utilization beyond main contract specifications in highly competitive markets.

Let F be a function that maps elements from K^n to K, where n and K are positive integers and a field, respectively. We investigate the condition under which f ∈ K[x] exhibits a specific property K with respect to the composition of polynomials, specifically the highest power of an integer n for which there exists an n-th composition iterand of f is exactly 1 if and only if the highest power of an integer K that f exhibits is also exhibited indefinitely. This paper focuses on extending this composition property iteratively, and as a consequence, demonstrates that the highest power of an integer N that  x^4+x^2+1  exhibits is infinite in the given field.

As the polar vortex on Saturn is transitioning from its phase with moderate seasonal changes to a more dramatic stage as summer approaches in its north pole, scientists observed a large oval enclosing the warm air current drifting counter-clockwise in the upper atmosphere. Using six decades' worth of infrared data from various sources, a six-thousand kilometer wide hexagonal pattern was discovered in the upper atmosphere during the northern hemisphere's summer season in March 2018, when the polar vortex started showing significant warming.

Consider a Schrödinger equation within an exterior region bounded by a convex set, featuring mass concentration below a critical threshold. The equation includes terms for potential, nonlinearity, and Cheeger constant, with solutions in a specific function space. Under the condition of no point mass, no explosion solutions arise for a general potential. However, when the domain and boundary allow for large domain decay, there exists a scenario where explosion solutions can occur despite the domain's size. Additionally, when the domain does not allow for significant domain decay and the convex set has a compact boundary, the nonexistence of explosion solutions is demonstrated when a specific potential-related condition is met. These findings also hold true in the context of the Schrödinger equation with source terms.

The concept of a -reduction of an ideal in a polynomial ring is explored, with parameters considered in either a characteristic zero or positive characteristic setting. Specifically, in the latter case, the properties of these ideals are examined, focusing on their primary decomposition and invariance under certain conditions. Additionally, the framework of semi-parametric local uniform reductions (sp-lur) is introduced to provide a stable ideal in a relevant quotient ring, with examples provided over various types of localizations of the rational numbers. Ultimately, the paper aims to establish existence proofs for sp-lur ideals in certain varieties defined over finite rings.

A linear bundle is an extension of a bundle by its own fiber, giving it a sheaf structure similar to that of a Lie algebroid. A "linear" bundle can be defined in two ways: either the base bundle consists of linear bundles or the fiber bundle consists of linear modules. A graded bundle is an extension of a bundle by multiple degrees, serving as a general framework for both linear bundles. A key feature of any connected graded bundle is an inverse one-to-one correspondence between its middle degree structure and its highest structure, mapping isotropic duals under the Kirillov–Coste–Weil (KCW) bracket. The KCW bracket, a general framework for Poincaré–Cartan and Hamilton structures, provides the underlying bracket for this relationship. A symplectic graded bundle is defined as a graded bundle with an inverse isotropic dual under the KCW bracket. A Lagrangian graded bundle is an isotropic dual of itself under the KCW bracket. A coisotropic graded bundle is an inclusion of an isotropic dual under the KCW bracket. A connection on a graded bundle is defined as an isomorphism between a lower bundle and a fiber bundle.
